steps.say: Autoantibodies cause disease when tolerance breaks down. Genetic risk plus a trigger indicates which autoreactive cells survive. Plasma cells then produce antibodies against our own tissues. This figure illustrates the path from trigger to tissue damage. Each antibody below is a marker of a different disease.
steps.tx: Autoimmunity begins when immune **tolerance** (the system that deletes self reactive lymphocytes) breaks down. Genetic risk plus an environmental trigger lets autoreactive T cells and B cells survive. Plasma cells then secrete **autoantibodies** (antibodies aimed at the body's own molecules) that deposit in tissue, fix complement, and recruit inflammation. Each antibody below marks a different disease, so match the antibody to the clinical picture.

vis.alt: Diagram of autoimmune pathogenesis from genetic and environmental triggers through loss of tolerance and autoreactive cells to pathogenic autoantibodies and tissue damage.
vis.caption: Loss of tolerance turns triggers into autoreactive cells and tissue injury. Each antibody later in this lesson sits at the end of this path. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: ANA screening uses HEp-2 cells with a 1 to 160 cutoff. Higher dilutions indicate stronger reactions. Anti double stranded DNA tracks lupus kidney flares. Anti Smith is rare but nearly diagnostic. You should remember which marker follows activity and which one only confirms the diagnosis.
steps.tx: Antinuclear antibody (**ANA**) testing by indirect immunofluorescence (a method that stains antibodies on HEp-2 cell substrates) is the screening test for systemic lupus erythematosus (a multisystem autoimmune disease). A titre of **1:160** or higher counts as significant in the 2019 ACR/EULAR criteria, with sensitivity above 98 percent. Anti double stranded DNA (**anti-dsDNA**) is over 95 percent specific, falls and rises with lupus nephritis (kidney inflammation) activity, and consumes complement. Anti Smith (**anti-Sm**, against core snRNP proteins) is 99 percent specific but does not track flares.

rows: No, titre alone does not track flares

steps.say: Anti-Ro crosses the placenta and can block the fetal heart. Complete heart block occurs in only 2 percent of exposed babies. Anti-La is present in most of the same patients. Both are also markers of Sjogren syndrome and skin lupus. Pregnancy plans require review whenever these antibodies are positive.
steps.tx: Anti Ro/SSA (against Ro60 and Ro52 proteins) and anti La/SSB antibodies mark **Sjogren syndrome** (autoimmune dry eyes and dry mouth disease) and subacute cutaneous lupus (a photosensitive annular rash). In pregnancy, maternal anti Ro/SSA crosses the **placenta** (the organ joining mother and fetus) and injures the fetal conduction system. About **2 percent** of exposed pregnancies develop neonatal lupus with congenital third degree heart block (complete electrical block needing a pacemaker). Screen every anti Ro positive pregnancy with serial fetal echocardiography.

points: Anti-Ro and anti-La mark Sjogren and skin lupus
left.title: Do

points: Assume most exposed babies develop block
Stop surveillance after one normal scan
right.title: Do not

steps.say: Anti-CCP is the specific early marker of rheumatoid arthritis. It appears years before swollen joints and predicts erosions. Rheumatoid factor is less specific and rises in infections and old age. Guidelines require both tests, and anti-CCP decides the diagnosis when they disagree.
steps.tx: Anti cyclic citrullinated peptide (**anti-CCP**) antibodies are 95 to 98 percent specific for rheumatoid arthritis (a chronic symmetric erosive joint disease). They appear years before **synovitis** (inflamed joint lining) and predict aggressive erosive damage, so positive patients need early intensive therapy. Rheumatoid factor (an IgM antibody against the Fc portion of human IgG) is less specific and occurs in hepatitis C, subacute bacterial endocarditis (heart valve infection), and healthy elderly people. A high titre anti-CCP with negative rheumatoid factor still means rheumatoid arthritis.

rows: Lower, rises in infection and age
Positive in hepatitis C and endocarditis

steps.say: The ANCA pattern points to the target antigen. Cytoplasmic staining indicates anti proteinase 3 and GPA. Perinuclear staining indicates anti myeloperoxidase and microscopic polyangiitis. Every pattern requires confirmation with antigen testing, since infections and drugs can mimic either pattern.
steps.tx: Antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (**ANCA**) patterns on ethanol fixed neutrophils point to the antigen. Cytoplasmic ANCA (**c-ANCA**, diffuse granular cytoplasmic staining) targets proteinase 3 (**PR3**, a neutrophil granule enzyme) and occurs in over 85 percent of active generalized granulomatosis with polyangiitis (a necrotizing small vessel disease). Perinuclear ANCA (**p-ANCA**, rim staining around the nucleus) targets myeloperoxidase (**MPO**) and predominates in microscopic polyangiitis and eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis. Confirm each pattern with PR3 and MPO immunoassays.

vis.alt: Clinical and histological panel of ANCA associated small vessel vasculitis showing granulomatous inflammation, crescentic glomerulonephritis, and pulmonary capillaritis.
vis.caption: c-ANCA with anti-PR3 marks GPA while p-ANCA with anti-MPO marks microscopic polyangiitis. Histology shows crescents and granulomas. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Each scleroderma antibody indicates the organ at risk. Centromere is the marker of limited skin disease with later lung vessel disease. Scl-70 is the marker of diffuse skin disease with lung fibrosis. RNA polymerase 3 is the marker of renal crisis and cancer. Every new patient requires the full panel plus screening of the predicted organ.
steps.tx: In systemic sclerosis (a fibrosing disease of skin and organs), **anti-centromere** antibodies mark limited cutaneous disease with late pulmonary arterial hypertension (high lung vessel pressure). Anti topoisomerase I (**anti-Scl-70**) marks diffuse cutaneous disease with interstitial lung disease (lung scarring). Anti **RNA polymerase III** marks diffuse disease with scleroderma renal crisis (malignant hypertension with kidney failure) and synchronous malignancy. Match each new scleroderma patient to one antibody, then screen the predicted organ on schedule.

steps.say: Anti-Jo-1 identifies the antisynthetase syndrome of muscle, lung, and hands. Anti-Mi-2 is the marker of classic rashes that show good treatment responses. Anti-TIF1-gamma indicates hidden cancer. In lupus, anti ribosomal P indicates psychosis risk. Weakness with lung disease requires the full myositis panel.
steps.tx: Anti Jo-1 (anti histidyl tRNA synthetase) defines the **antisynthetase syndrome**: myositis (muscle inflammation) with interstitial lung disease, Raynaud phenomenon (cold induced colour change), non erosive arthritis, and **mechanic's hands** (cracked hyperkeratotic fingertips). Anti Mi-2 marks classic dermatomyositis while anti **TIF1-gamma** flags malignancy associated myositis. In lupus, anti **ribosomal P** (against P0, P1, and P2 proteins) associates with acute psychosis, depression, and severe hepatic involvement. Test these panels when weakness, rash, or psychosis meets systemic disease.

vis.alt: Mechanic's hands with cracked hyperkeratotic skin along the fingertips in antisynthetase syndrome.
vis.caption: Cracked fingertips of mechanic's hands point to anti-Jo-1 disease with lung involvement. Anti-TIF1-gamma instead points to cancer. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Clinicians use ANA to screen, specific antibodies to confirm, and activity markers to follow flares. A lone positive ANA is never treated as lupus. The pregnancy question is never skipped with anti-Ro. Cancer screening is never forgotten with anti-TIF1-gamma or RNA polymerase 3.
steps.tx: Use ANA to screen, specific antibodies to confirm, and activity markers to follow. The exam traps are fixed: a lone positive **ANA** without features is not lupus, anti-dsDNA flares need escalation while anti-Sm needs none, a 2 percent heart block risk still needs full fetal surveillance, and anti **TIF1-gamma** or anti RNA polymerase III needs a malignancy hunt. Order the antibody that answers the question in front of you, then act on the organ it predicts.
